holding_summary: In a homestead-partition dispute, the court held that a 21-unit tourist court built and operated by the widow on the same tract as her residence constituted both her personal and business homestead, exempt from partition, because operating and renting the cabins occupied all of her time and effort as an ordinary business. The court treated running a tourist court renting cabins by the day or week as no different in kind from operating a grocery store, gristmill, or print shop.

quotes.text: the evidence conclusively reveals that the land was purchased for the purpose of establishing thereon a tourist court to be occupied as a personal and business homestead

is that which occupies the time, labor, and efforts of its owner or operator, and we think it is doing no violence to the term to say that operating a tourist camp is as distinctive a business as operating a grocery store, a gristmill, or a print shop.

notes: Characterization left null: the court classifies the tourist-court operation as a homestead 'business' for exemption purposes; it does not characterize the occupants' stays as lease/license/lodging/innkeeping.

Dispute over a movie-theater parking-lot variance under a zoning ordinance; 'boarding house' appears only as one item in a list of uses permitted in a second residential district. No discussion of letting/lodging legal character or regulation.

Homestead-abandonment/estoppel dispute over a mortgaged duplex whose apartments were rented by the month or week for revenue; the rental facts are background to the estoppel holding, and the court never rules on the legal character or regulation of the letting itself. Milner v. Scottish holding discussed within (a 'rooming house' plan) is cited precedent, not this case's own holding.

Dispute over enforceability of an ice-manufacturing-plant zoning restriction. 'Boarding house'/'apartment district' appear only within the ordinance's list of permitted uses; no bearing on lodging's legal character or regulation as such.

Fire-insurance coverage dispute turning on a policy clause requiring the building be 'occupied by owner'; concerns whether a tenant's (vs. owner's) full occupancy voids coverage, not short-term room/lodger letting or its regulation.

Arson conviction reversed for insufficient evidence; a tourist camp is mentioned only as the alibi location where defendant registered for the night. No bearing on lodging's legal character or regulation.
Burglary conviction; a tourist camp in Georgetown is mentioned only as a stopover en route to the burglary. No bearing on lodging law.
Theft-of-whiskey conviction reversed on principal-actor grounds; a Wichita Falls tourist camp is mentioned only as the cabin where stolen whiskey was stored. No bearing on lodging law.
Robbery-by-assault conviction affirmed; a Longview tourist camp cabin is mentioned only as the scene of an earlier unrelated incident recounted by the defendant. No bearing on lodging law.
Armed-robbery conviction affirmed; a Fort Worth tourist camp is mentioned only as the place where the fleeing defendant reunited with his wife and was arrested. No bearing on lodging law.

Assault-with-intent-to-murder conviction affirmed; a tourist camp is mentioned only as where the complaining witness had lived with the defendant's ex-husband during an affair. No bearing on lodging law.
Habeas challenge to a municipal anti-loitering ordinance near schools/public buildings, held void; unrelated to lodging, boarding houses, or short-term letting.
Liquor-sale conviction reversed on jury-voir-dire grounds; defendant is noted only as one who 'conducted a tourist camp,' with no litigation over the lodging operation itself.
Murder conviction affirmed; the Waco Tourist Camp is mentioned only as the location of the killing. No bearing on lodging law.
Rape conviction reversed on cross-examination grounds; the Tri-State Camp is mentioned only as where the underage prosecutrix and a companion lived. No bearing on lodging law.
Retrial/appeal of the same liquor-sale defendant who 'conducted a tourist camp'; the appeal concerns jury and evidentiary issues, not the lodging operation's legal character or regulation.

Rape conviction reversed for exclusion of newly discovered evidence; an Oklahoma tourist camp is mentioned only as where the prosecutrix allegedly spent a night with another man. No bearing on lodging law.

Illegal-liquor-possession conviction affirmed; the searched premises is a 'tourist camp under control and supervision of appellant,' but the appeal concerns the search warrant and juror misconduct, not the lodging operation's legal character or regulation.
